notes: No dedicated anti-cruelty statute for companion/domestic animals. Protection is patchwork via Wildlife Protection Law (captive-bred wildlife only), Criminal Law Art. 341 (protected wildlife only), Public Security Administration Punishment Law Art. 89 (nuisance/dangerous dogs, NOT a cruelty provision), Animal Epidemic Prevention Law and its own Implementing Regulations (both disease-control/procedural only, confirmed twice to contain zero welfare content), and a wider sub-national patchwork coded 2026-09-15: a 2020-02-24 NPC Standing Committee Decision banning wildlife consumption (the national legal trigger, anchoring the wildlife/livestock boundary to a livestock catalogue) prompted Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Guangzhou, and Beijing to each pass supporting local legislation within about two months, all excluding cats/dogs by omission from a food-species whitelist rather than naming them, contrary to widespread media framing - Beijing folded its version into a comprehensive wildlife-law rewrite rather than a narrow ordinance. Shanghai, by contrast, repealed its old wildlife law in this same 2020 window but did not pass a replacement until 2023-06-20, operating without any local implementing regulation for over three years. Separately, Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and (per secondary sources) Chengdu have municipal dog-keeping ordinances explicitly prohibiting abusing/abandoning a dog - though Beijing's and Shanghai's abuse prohibitions carry no attached penalty of any kind, an enforcement gap verified by checking every cross-reference in each ordinance's penalty chapter, while Guangzhou's and Beijing's own separate wildlife-abuse duty (in its wildlife ordinance, not its dog ordinance) do carry real fines. A voluntary (non-mandatory) national technical standard for zoos, CJJ/T 263-2017, explicitly names animal welfare as a purpose and bans using wildlife for performances, but has no independent enforcement mechanism and a documented history (per a 2013 People's Daily report) of a predecessor MOHURD document going unenforced as "a dead letter." No welfare-relevant regulation could be located for circuses/animal-performance troupes at all (a different ministry has jurisdiction there) - a confirmed regulatory gap. A national comprehensive anti-cruelty law has been proposed by NPC delegates and academics since at least 2009 but has never advanced past the proposal stage (confirmed current as of 2026-09-15).
Animal Protection Act 1998 (動物保護法), amended repeatedly; major penalty-raising amendment 2017-04-26 (often mis-cited as 2015). Central authority 農業部 (MOA); nationwide hotline 1959 since 2022.

Cap. 169 Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Ordinance (1935); maximum penalty last raised in 2006, NOT 2023/2024 as some sources claim. Reform package (duty-of-care offence, indictable tier) under consultation since 2019, still unenacted as of Feb 2026. SPCA HK has no delegated statutory enforcement power.

Law No. 4/2016 (動物保護法), Macau's first dedicated animal-protection law. Access to primary/secondary sources severely restricted this session (bo.io.gov.mo, iam.gov.mo unreachable) - most fields below general_offence unverified.

Act on Welfare and Management of Animals 1973 (動物の愛護及び管理に関する法律); major 2019 reform staged through June 2022/2023/2024. Official English translation is stale (reflects only the 2005 text). Enforcement: MOE sets standards, prefectural welfare centers + police investigate.

Animal Protection Act 1991 (동물보호법); comprehensive 2022 revision (effective 2023-2024) raised top penalty to 3yr/30M won, criminalized abuse-footage distribution. 2024 dog-meat phase-out special act (separate law). Dogfighting not independently criminalized - only via the gambling provision, a documented loophole.

Animals and Birds Act 1965 (Cap. 7), Part IV ss.41-48; major 2014 amendment effective 2015-01-16 added duty-of-care offence and disqualification orders. SPCA Singapore has no statutory enforcement power. Wildlife handled separately under the Wildlife Act 1965.

No general federal anti-cruelty offence - general cruelty/neglect/abandonment is exclusively state law. Federal statutes are narrow and commerce-tied: 18 U.S.C. §48 (animal crushing, expanded by the PACT Act 2019) and the Animal Welfare Act (7 U.S.C. §2131, licensed-facility standards only, with a narrow, exclusion-heavy definition of covered animals).

Criminal Code ss.444-447.1 contains a genuinely general cruelty offence (s.445.1(1)(a)) with national reach - unlike the US. Note the internal inconsistency: s.446 (neglect/duty-of-care) caps at 2yr indictable while ss.445/445.1/447 cap at 5yr. Enforcement is provincial; Ontario abolished its private-charity (OSPCA) model in 2020 in favor of a government Animal Welfare Services body (PAWS Act).

Animal Welfare Act 2006 (ss.4 unnecessary suffering, s.9 duty of care); Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021 raised max penalty from 6mo to 5yr; Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act 2022 is a SEPARATE policy-scrutiny mechanism covering cephalopods/decapods, does NOT alter the 2006 Act's criminal-offence scope. RSPCA is the dominant private prosecutor.

Animal Health and Welfare (Scotland) Act 2006, same dual unnecessary-suffering/duty-of-care structure. Animals and Wildlife (Penalties, Protections and Powers) (Scotland) Act 2020 raised max to 5yr/£20,000 summary cap (NOT titled a 'sentencing and sentience' act - correcting a common misattribution). Scottish SPCA is a REPORTING agency to COPFS, not a private prosecutor like RSPCA.

Welfare of Animals Act (Northern Ireland) 2011, ss.4/9/14 mirror the England & Wales structure. Enforcement split: DAERA (farmed animals), district councils (companion/kept animals, can prosecute), PSNI (wildlife/fighting/crime-linked cases). USPCA appears to function as an investigative/referral charity, NOT a private prosecutor equivalent to RSPCA - unconfirmed either way.

No EU-level criminal offence exists; TFEU Art. 13 is a cross-cutting sentience-mainstreaming policy principle, and Directive 98/58/EC imposes only a result obligation on member states (excludes invertebrates). Present as a framework/harmonization layer, not a peer 'anti-cruelty statute' entry. 2023-2026 Animal Welfare Package (dogs/cats traceability regulation) near-final adoption as of Sept 2026, exact date unresolved.

Tierschutzgesetz (TierSchG) 1972, current consolidated version 2006 (amended 2022). §17 criminal offence covers VERTEBRATES ONLY, requires intent (negligence/attempt not punishable), and has no aggravated/qualified tier - a 2024 bill to add one died with the legislative period and the current coalition excludes reform. No official English translation confirmed current.

Code pénal art. 521-1 et seq., substantially reformed by Loi n°2021-1539 (2021-11-30) which raised sentencing tiers, added sexual-abuse offences (art.521-1-1/2/3) and a filming/broadcasting offence (art.39). Code civil art.515-14 (2015) recognizes animal sentience without granting legal personality - animals remain 'biens' (property).

Tierschutzgesetz (TSchG) 2005, in force 2008. Art. 2 is an explicit statutory enabling clause: the law applies to vertebrates, with the Federal Council empowered to extend coverage to invertebrates by ordinance based on scientific evidence of suffering capacity. Cantonal veterinarian-led enforcement (Art.33); a keeping-ban issued by one canton is valid nationwide via a federal (BLV) registry.

Wet dieren (Animals Act) 2011. Article 1.3 codifies the animal's 'intrinsieke waarde' (inherent value) as a sentient being, binding on all state rulemaking. Standalone 'houdverbod' (ownership ban, up to 30yr or life for serious/repeat cases) became available from 2024-01-01. Exact statutory maximum criminal penalty is unresolved (conflicting sources cite 3yr vs 5yr).

Codice Penale Titolo IX-bis (arts.544-bis to 544-sexies), inserted 2004. Legge 82/2025 ('legge Brambilla'), in force since 2025-07-01, is the first major reform in 20+ years - RENAMED the title from 'crimes against the sentiment for animals' to 'crimes against animals', reframing animals themselves (not human sentiment) as the protected legal interest.

Dual 2023 reform: Ley 7/2023 (welfare framework, in force 2023-09-29) EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES hunting dogs, bullfighting animals, livestock, and several other working-animal categories from its general protections. Ley Orgánica 3/2023 (in force 2023-04-18) repealed old Código Penal art.337 and replaced it with arts.340 bis-quinquies - citations to 'art.337' as current are now an error.

No federal animal-cruelty statute; welfare is constitutionally a state/territory responsibility. The Australian Animal Welfare Standards and Guidelines (AAWS&G) are explicitly non-binding until a state/territory enacts them.

Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1979. s.5 general cruelty / s.6 aggravated cruelty. 'Animal' = vertebrate species; crustaceans covered ONLY in a food-preparation/consumption context, not generally. RSPCA NSW, Animal Welfare League NSW, the Greyhound Welfare Integrity Commission, and NSW Police are the authorised enforcers.

Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1986 (current compilation v097, effective 2025-10-22). A promised replacement 'Animal Care and Protection Bill' (committed 2017, consultation 2021) was confirmed SHELVED for 2026 in March 2026 - POCTA 1986 remains the operative statute with no confirmed replacement timeline.

Animal Welfare Act 1999, amended 2015 (broadened enforcement powers, stronger standards). Primary statutory text (sections, penalties, exact scope) could NOT be verified this session - legislation.govt.nz was unreachable by every method tried (~10 attempts). MPI and RNZSPCA jointly enforce.

Penal Code sec.597 is a felony-eligible "wobbler" applying identically to active cruelty (subd.a/c) AND passive neglect (subd.b), with no prior-conviction gate - broader than the popular "felony on first offense" framing usually implies, since it reaches neglect too. Cross-checked against ALDF's 2025 rankings (Oregon #1) and confirmed California is NOT top-5 nationally on ALDF's holistic ~20-category scoring despite this specific structural feature being real - a good example of one true statutory feature not supporting a broader "strongest law" claim. Distinctive dual-track enforcement, coded hybrid: government county/city Animal Control Officers (Penal Code sec.830.9, exercise peace-officer arrest powers within their employing jurisdiction only) alongside privately-employed Humane Officers individually confirmed by a superior court judge (Corporations Code sec.14502, via a formal fingerprint/background-check/insurance/court-petition process) whose statewide enforcement authority is not geographically bounded the way an Animal Control Officer's is - a more formally judicially-supervised public/private co-enforcement structure than the "hybrid" value was originally designed to describe for other jurisdictions.

Maintains TWO SEPARATE cruelty statutes with different scopes and penalty schedules that cross-reference each other for recidivism purposes: Penal Code sec.42.092 (non-livestock: domesticated animals including stray/feral cats and dogs, plus previously-captured wild animals) and sec.42.09 (livestock only, a distinct and narrower conduct list). First-offence felony exposure for intentional torture/killing (third-degree felony, 2-10 years) is more than triple California's ceiling for equivalent conduct, escalating to 2-20 years (second-degree felony) with one qualifying prior - the highest criminal exposure of any jurisdiction in this database. "Pancho's Law" (H.B. 285), effective 2025-09-01, recently added a criminal-negligence mens rea standard to sec.42.092(b), closing a gap where serious harm from carelessness (not intent/knowledge/recklessness) previously fell outside the statute. Enforcement_model coded police_administrative as the closest fit, but this understates a genuinely decentralized reality: no dedicated state agency and no California-style statewide private-humane-officer-commissioning framework was found - enforcement is a county-by-county patchwork of sheriff's offices, some dedicated city police units (e.g. Dallas), and some counties contracting a local SPCA chapter for a deputized position.

The Provincial Animal Welfare Services Act, 2019 (PAWS Act) replaced the private-charity OSPCA enforcement model with a government inspectorate in 2020 - independently verified (previously only snippet-tier via secondary report in this database's CA-FED notes). A genuinely novel textual finding: the word "cruelty" appears in the Act exactly 6 times, every occurrence referencing the OLD, REPEALED "Ontario Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act" - the PAWS Act itself never uses "cruelty" as an operative legal term, building its entire offence structure instead on the undefined-breadth concept of "distress." The Act also contains NO statutory definition of "animal" at all, unlike jurisdictions (e.g. NSW/Victoria) that expressly limit scope to vertebrates. The Chief Animal Welfare Inspector and appointed inspectors sit under the Solicitor General (a public-safety/policing ministry, not agriculture) and hold real coercive powers: warrantless entry for animals in critical distress, warrant/telewarrant inspection, warrantless seizure, and forfeiture.

Quebec is a civil-law jurisdiction, unlike the rest of common-law Canada. Its widely-cited 2015 Civil Code reform (Art.898.1: "Animals are not property. They are sentient beings with biological needs") creates NO offence, penalty, or enforcement mechanism of its own - verified directly, and confirmed by a Quebec legal commentary source that independently reaches the same conclusion. ALL penalties trace to a separate statute passed by the SAME 2015 omnibus act: the Animal Welfare and Safety Act (BWSA, chapter B-3.1), administered by MAPAQ (the agriculture ministry, staffed by veterinarians/agronomists per the Act's own definition of "inspecteur") - a genuinely different institutional placement than Ontario's policing-ministry model despite both provinces independently converging on "distress"/"bien-être compromis" (not "cruelty") as their core operative standard within the same decade. The single most distinctive finding in this database: BWSA provides NO IMPRISONMENT for a first offence at any severity - even a first-offence conviction for causing an animal's death is fine-only; imprisonment exists only as a doubling/tripling recidivist-fine enhancement (6-18 months, repeat offences only).

The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act (PCAA) is enforced by the BC SPCA - but this is a materially more government-embedded arrangement than a plain "private charity enforces" hybrid: the Society is statutorily CONTINUED as a body corporate by the Act itself (s.3, not merely contracted), the Minister can DISALLOW or unilaterally rewrite the Society's own enforcement-policy bylaws (s.6), individual officers must hold special-provincial-constable status under the Police Act (s.10) - a materially stronger sworn-officer designation than England's RSPCA inspectors hold - and appeals go to an independent government tribunal, the BC Farm Industry Review Board (Part 3.1). Operative offence vocabulary is uniformly "distress" (s.1(2)), never "cruelty" as an offence element, DESPITE the Act's own title and the Society's own name both retaining "Cruelty" - unlike Ontario, which dropped the word entirely when it replaced its own former OSPCA-based model. Penalty is a SINGLE FLAT maximum (,000/2 years) with NO severity tiering at all - even obstructing an enforcement officer carries the identical ceiling as the worst cruelty offence, a genuinely distinct structure from every other jurisdiction in this database. This penalty ceiling and the 3-year limitation period both trace directly to the 2010 Whistler sled-dog cull (approx. 100 dogs killed by an employee of a tour operator) and the resulting 2011 government Sled Dog Task Force reform - a rare case in this database of a law's current numbers being traceable to one specific precipitating scandal. A 2023 government-commissioned Farmed Animal Welfare Advisory Committee recommended moving farmed-animal enforcement toward a dedicated Ministry of Agriculture inspectorate function - unimplemented as of 2026, but a live signal of the same private-to-government pressure Ontario resolved in 2020.

The Animal Protection Act (APA) is, as of 2026-09-16, mid-transition: Bill 22 (the Animal Protection Amendment Act, 2026) received Royal Assent 2026-05-14 but is NOT YET PROCLAIMED into force, so the CURRENTLY OPERATIVE law is the pre-Bill-22 text - see provisions notes for the specific pending-vs-current penalty figures. Enforcement is split THREE WAYS by geography among legally separate organizations under one agency-agnostic statutory peace-officer clause (the Act itself names no enforcing body): the Alberta SPCA (a rural charity, ~12 peace officers province-wide outside the two major cities), Calgary Humane Society (a DIFFERENT private charity, city-specific), and the City of Edmonton (municipal government employees, since the Edmonton Humane Society withdrew from its enforcement contract in 2018 citing inability to meet tightened provincial standards - a genuine micro-analogue to Ontario's 2020 provincewide OSPCA-to-government transition, but occurring a year earlier, at municipal rather than provincial scale, and leaving Alberta MORE fragmented rather than consolidating enforcement). The Alberta SPCA's own public statement calls its governing statute "the oldest and weakest in Canada... last updated in 2005" - independently corroborated by the Act's own section-history footnotes. Operative offence vocabulary is "distress" (s.1(2)) - "cruelty" appears exactly once in the whole Act, as a humane-society-approval criterion, never as an offence element.
